title: Pinned 還是 Plain end？捲軸鋸片買錯的那一步
summary: 捲軸鋸片有兩種接頭：帶銷（pinned）與平頭（plain end）。買錯不是效能差一點，是根本裝不上去。這篇講怎麼看自己的機器、兩種接頭各自適合什麼工作，以及能不能互換。
body:
「我的機器要用哪一種？」——這是我們最常收到的捲軸鋸片問題，而且十次有八次，問的人手上已經買錯一包。原因很簡單：兩種接頭長得幾乎一樣，但機構不相容。

先分清楚兩種接頭

帶銷（Pinned end）：鋸片兩端各有一根橫向的小銷，卡在機器上下夾頭的凹槽裡。安裝只要「勾上去、鎖緊」，不需要工具，適合入門機與快速換片。

平頭（Plain end）：兩端是平整的薄片，靠夾頭的螺絲或快夾壓住。優點是可以從鑽孔穿過去做內部鏤空，而且能用到更細的規格。

PinnedPlain end
安裝卡銷入槽，免工具夾頭壓緊，通常要鎖螺絲
最短可用長度受銷距限制（常見 5 吋）可短到 3 吋以下
內部鏤空不行（銷卡不進鑽孔）可以（先鑽孔再穿線）
常見齒數10–18 TPI10–28 TPI
適合入門、快速直線與曲線切割精細木工、模型、內輪廓

怎麼看自己的機器吃哪一種

不用查型號，看上夾頭就好：

  • 夾頭是一個 U 型槽 + 彈簧片，鋸片銷直接掉進凹槽 → 這是 pinned 機。
  • 夾頭是兩片金屬 + 螺絲（或快夾扳手），把薄片夾住 → 這是 plain end 機，也叫 pinless。

不確定就把舊鋸片抽出來看：兩端有橫銷就是 pinned，沒有就是 plain。

買錯了怎麼辦

有兩種補救，視機器而定：

  1. 換夾頭：多數 16 吋以上的機器可以換成 pinless 夾頭（改裝件），換完就能用平頭鋸片，等於升級。
  2. 換機器：入門機的夾頭多半焊死，改裝不划算。這時候就認命買 pinned——它沒有比較差，只是上限低一點。

反過來，plain end 的機器不建議硬裝 pinned：銷會被夾頭壓歪，鋸片跑偏、斷片，還會傷夾頭。

齒數怎麼配

捲軸鋸的齒數比手鋸密，因為它切的是薄料與曲線：

  • 軟木、合板 3 mm 以下：18–28 TPI，切口細、毛邊少。
  • 一般木材 5–20 mm：10–15 TPI，排屑快、轉彎順。
  • 壓克力、塑膠、薄金屬：18 TPI 以上，慢速進給，避免熔膠或撕裂。

一個實務經驗：轉彎半徑小的時候，齒數越高越好轉，因為每一齒吃掉的料少，比較不會卡在曲線上。

採購時的兩個提醒

第一，問清楚「pin 距」（兩端銷中心到中心的距離），不同品牌差 1–2 mm 就裝不進去，光看「5 吋」不夠。第二，確認包裝標示的接頭型別——我們出貨會在彩盒與外箱都標 PINNED / PLAIN，OEM 客戶可以指定要哪一種標法。
title_en: Pinned or Plain End? The Scroll Saw Blade Mistake Buyers Keep Making
summary_en: Scroll saw blades come with two very different ends: pinned and plain. Choosing wrong is not a small performance loss — the blade will not fit at all. Here is how to check your machine, what each type is good for, and whether you can convert.
body_en:
"Which blade does my saw take?" is the question we get most often about scroll saw blades — and eight times out of ten, the person asking has already bought the wrong pack. The reason is simple: the two ends look almost identical, but the mechanisms are not compatible.

The two types

Pinned end: each end carries a small cross pin that drops into a slot in the upper and lower clamps. No tools, instant blade changes, and the usual choice on entry-level saws.

Plain end: the ends are flat strips gripped by thumbscrews or a quick-release clamp. The advantage is that the blade can be threaded through a drilled hole for interior cutouts, and it can go down to much finer sizes.

PinnedPlain end
FittingPin drops into a slot, tool-freeClamp grips the flat end, usually a screw
Shortest bladeLimited by pin spacing (often 5 in)Down to 3 in or less
Interior cutoutsNo — the pin will not pass a drilled holeYes — drill, thread, re-clamp
Typical TPI10–1810–28
Best forEntry-level saws, fast curved cutsFine woodwork, models, inside profiles

How to tell what your saw takes

You do not need the model number — just look at the upper clamp:

  • A U-shaped slot with a spring blade that the pin drops into → pinned machine.
  • Two metal jaws with a screw or a quick-release lever that pinch the blade → plain-end (pinless) machine.

Still unsure? Pull the old blade out: a cross pin at either end means pinned; a flat strip means plain.

If you already bought the wrong ones

  1. Change the clamps: most 16-inch and larger saws accept a pinless conversion kit, which also lets you use finer blades.
  2. Change the saw: entry-level clamps are usually fixed, and converting costs more than it is worth. Buy pinned blades — they are not inferior, just capped at a coarser range.

Going the other way is a bad idea: never force a pinned blade into a plain-end clamp. The pin gets crushed, the blade wanders and snaps, and the clamp is damaged.

Matching the tooth count

  • Softwood and plywood under 3 mm: 18–28 TPI for a clean, narrow kerf.
  • General wood 5–20 mm: 10–15 TPI clears chips and turns easily.
  • Acrylic, plastics, thin metal: 18 TPI or finer, slow feed to avoid melting or tearing.

One rule from the shop floor: the tighter the curve, the finer the blade. Fewer teeth per stroke means the blade is less likely to jam in a tight radius.

Two things to check before ordering

First, ask for the pin spacing — centre-to-centre distance between the pins. A 1–2 mm difference between brands is enough to stop the blade fitting, so "5 inch" on its own tells you nothing. Second, make sure the pack states the end type: we print PINNED / PLAIN on both the colour box and the carton, and OEM customers can specify how it is marked.
